Your buildings

Building selects an independent project with its own floors, rooms, connections and view. Manage lets you create, duplicate or rename a building, add or rename floors, File opens older layouts from Archive. L0 is the permanent ground-floor code; its name is editable. Undo and redo stay with the building while this tab is open.

Edits save locally in this browser on this device. File exports one building or a complete building backup. Import always creates new copies; it never replaces your current building. Keep a downloaded backup before clearing browser data or changing devices.

Stairs and floors

Stairs + creates an aligned stair stack across the floors you check. Select an existing room, then Convert to stairs in the inspector or its right-click menu to keep its footprint. Preview shows the required size, real elevations, flights, landings, skipped floor openings and any warnings before saving. Select an existing stair and choose Edit connected floors to extend its stack. Move and resize linked stairs together. New stairs still need doors into adjacent rooms at the floor arrival end. The stair inspector checks these doors against the landing.

The left floor list works like pages: click a floor, add one with +, or use Edit floor to rename it or change its elevation. Building management and the legacy archive are above the list. The Theme picker offers Light, Dark and Hybrid. Hybrid keeps light room colors on a dark canvas. Grid & snap in View sets the grid spacing for this building or turns it off. On a phone, Inspector lets you hide or show the detail panel for more drawing space.

Direct drawing tools

Press D to select the Door tool: hover to preview the exact opening, then click. Shared walls connect their rooms automatically; exposed walls connect to Outside. The tool stays active for repeated placements. Press V or Escape to return to selection. Use View to choose Single, Double or Open for new openings. Connection labels, including exterior entrance labels, can be renamed in their inspector or right-click menu.

Selection is the default, with an arrow cursor. Drag a box on empty canvas to select every room and doorway fully inside it. Shift-click adds or removes objects; Shift-drag a box toggles the enclosed objects. Drag a selected object or the group border to move the selection, and use its eight outer handles to resize. Each completed group drag is one Undo step; Escape restores it. Group resizing keeps door widths fixed, preserves shared walls inside the selection and moves linked stairs and source-derived footprints once. Protected footprints must be removed from a group before transforming. Connections to unselected rooms can become detached and are flagged for review. Select one object to edit its detailed properties or delete it. Drag a door or passage along its shared wall. Right-click a room to change its type, or a connection to change its type or delete it. The current type is checked. With a room or connection selected, Shift+F10 opens the same menu; use the arrow keys and Enter. Hold Space or use middle-mouse drag for temporary pan. Release Space to resume your previous tool. On touch screens, drag empty paper to pan and use two fingers on empty paper to zoom.

Press C to connect: drag from one room into an adjacent room, or across an exposed wall into empty space to add an exterior door. Tap a room then an adjacent room or empty space for the same action. A drag across a wall touching another room or void cannot make an exterior door. A green shared-wall preview shows a valid connection. Choose single door, double door or open passage in the always-visible Connections panel. Single doors start at 1.2 m and double doors at 2 m. Changing back to single resets its width to 1.2 m. The clear-width slider changes in 0.1 m steps and stays within the shared wall. A drag is one Undo step; Escape cancels it. Double doors have two leaves and a total clear width. Open passages have no door leaf.

Press X to disconnect: click a connection, or drag between two connected rooms. Press P to draw a room: drag a rectangle, using the selected grid spacing with a 1 × 1 m minimum. C, X, P and D select persistent tools. Releasing the key does not cancel a drag or change the tool. Press V to select; Escape cancels an unfinished edit and returns to selection. Clicking the active toolbar tool also returns to selection. Tool buttons stay active on touch screens.

Delete / Backspace removes the selected room or connection. Rooms without connections delete immediately. Other room deletions confirm how many connections will also be removed. Undo restores the entire change. Typing in fields never triggers drawing shortcuts.

Linked stairs move and resize together on every level in their stack; local transfer stairs stay local. Legacy misalignment is preserved until you explicitly edit that stack. Courtyard and Operations voids follow their source room and cannot be moved separately. Freight shafts retain their existing locks. Actual overlapping room areas are shown in red; intentional void/shaft cutouts are excluded. The lower-floor stack overlays each lower above-ground level at 10% opacity. Current floors are solid and mask the stack; real voids remain open. Basements show only lower basement levels. Toggle the stack and dimensions in View. File contains JSON/SVG export and import; level notes and the legend are in the inspector. Switching floors preserves your view. Stair flights, treads and landings are calculated from actual elevations; UP and DOWN routes are drawn separately. The stair inspector shows clear widths, risers and headroom checks. Required slab, services and ceiling cutouts remain design requirements; this is not a construction or runtime-traversal certification. Corridors are editable rooms too. Plan checks flag overlaps, detached doors and rooms without a route to a floor entrance.

Undo / redo: Ctrl or ⌘ Z / Shift Z. Arrow keys move by the selected grid size (0.1 m with snap off). SVG export produces editable vector linework for Figma; JSON preserves the complete editable model.
